target_customer: Spanish speaking aspiring developers in Latin America (students), and companies hiring remote tech talent
problem: Latin America has far more software openings than trained engineers, and training is unaffordable upfront. Henry trained students at zero upfront cost and recovered a share of future income.
business_model: Income share agreement bootcamp (15 percent of salary for 24 months, capped, per 2020 coverage), later a hiring fee from employers

founders.background_notes: From the YC page, which calls him a serial entrepreneur based in Argentina.

founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by the YC page, TechCrunch Dec 2020 (sibling of Martin) and an edtech article May 2022.

competitors.name: Microverse
competitors.what: YC backed income share bootcamp training people in developing countries

competitors.name: Lambda School
competitors.what: US income share coding school, the model Henry copied for Latin America
competitors.traction_then: 17 percent of salary for 24 months above $4,167 a month, capped at $30,000

technical_complexity.rationale: An online curriculum, cohorts and a hiring marketplace are operationally heavy but technically light; the hard part is selection and job placement.

defensibility.rationale: Spanish language focus, a 3 percent admit rate and an employer network (1,000+ companies by 2022) helped, but bootcamps and income share models are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Lambda reportedly failed to expand abroad (TechCrunch Dec 2020). No incumbent bought or copied Henry in the sources found.

market_need_then: Henry cited about 1 million software openings in Latin America against fewer than 100,000 trained professionals (TechCrunch Dec 2020), with 800+ students enrolled within months of its March 2020 launch.

branding.name_origin: One article (iProUP) says Henry stands for High Income, Not Rich Yet; single source, not confirmed by the company pages opened.
branding.domain_note: Uses soyhenry.com (Spanish for I am Henry) rather than henry.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Punchy copy such as 'Hire like Big Tech. Pay like a startup.' (current site)

branding.brand_signature: #SoyHenry student identity and hashtag, used by the CEO in a March 2021 tweet (search result)
branding.community_and_virality: Graduates describe learning inside a community; 20K+ graduates are claimed by the company.

brand_strength.rationale: A human name with a student identity hashtag, a memorable acronym story and regional press, though a single article supports the origin and no mascot or merch was found.

pivots.from: Income share agreement bootcamp for students
pivots.to: Vetted AI engineer talent for hiring companies with a flat fee per hire
pivots.why: Not stated; current site sells shortlists and a USD 3,000 hire fee. Date approximate from the page and the AI tags, not from a source.

outcome_analysis: Henry launched in March 2020, enrolled 800+ students quickly, raised $1.5M seed in December 2020 and a $10M Series A in May 2022, reaching 5,000+ students and 1,000+ hiring companies. It now claims 20K graduates and sells vetted AI talent to employers. No exit or later round was found, so the story is steady growth for a Latin American edtech with a model proven by Lambda School.
notes: YC batch is Summer 2020 per the YC page; Forbes Colombia suggests a 2019 selection process, sources differ. The Series A is dated May 2022 (edtechreview May 5, Forbes May 3 2022 per YC news links). The pivot date is approximate and unsourced. The unsourced 2024 pivot is inferred from the current site only. Founding year uses the March 2020 launch.
